protocol.status: Exploratory follow-up after a source sensor-relation audit; not an untouched final holdout.
protocol.hypothesis_source: outputs/sensor_relation_audit.json; no results from the four-detector comparison used to choose parameters.
protocol.formula: activePower_mean = intercept + coefficient * sum(voltage_phase_mean * current_phase_mean), phases R/S/T.
protocol.calibration: Reuse run_experiment.calibrate with March1-15 absolute residual scores only; budget 0.5/1/2 events per observed equipment day.
protocol.score: Absolute contemporaneous observed-power minus learned relation-predicted-power residual.
protocol.score_unit: W under source activePower unit assumption; source specification confirmation remains pending.
protocol.comparison_minutes: Exactly build_features(frame).valid, including five past complete minutes and midnight/gap resets.
protocol.decision_time: End of third consecutive flagged complete minute.
protocol.synthetic: Reuse the same generator, training-only sensor scales, seed, rule-safe paired controls, amended directions and max_per_type=1 per equipment.
protocol.results_interpretation: Report event counts and flagged-time burden, paired synthetic recall/delay and baseline pre-existing alerts. No real-fault precision/recall claim.
limitations: Contemporaneous cross-sensor consistency is not future forecasting.
Product of minute means differs from mean of products; aggregation covariance contributes to residual.
A learned coefficient absorbs source conventions; it is not a verified electrical conversion factor.
Coherent current and power changes can stay on the relation and be missed.
Changes in within-minute variability without changed means are intentionally invisible to this relation score.
Sensor inconsistencies can produce a residual without equipment damage.
April and source audit are development data; new real data and human-confirmed events remain necessary.
